statement:
A first-order thickening of ringed topoi is a morphism $i:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O')$ whose direct-image functor identifies the underlying topoi and whose structure-sheaf map $\mathcal O'\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O$ is surjective with square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Under this identification $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O$-module. A general thickening requires only a locally nilpotent kernel.

For a first-order thickening of ringed topoi, an extension of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal K$ means a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to0$ of $\mathcal O'$-modules, where $\mathcal I$ annihilates the end terms. Such an extension induces the map $c_{\mathcal F'}:\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F\to\mathcal K$ given by multiplication on local lifts.

Let $i : (\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}')$
be a first order thickening of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be $\mathcal{O}'$-modules.
Set $\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$ and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{G}'$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-linear map.
The set of lifts of $\varphi$ to an $\mathcal{O}'$-linear map
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$ is, if nonempty, a principal
homogeneous space under
$\operatorname{Hom}_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}')$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}'$ is an $\mathcal{O}'$-module of finite presentation, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\mathcal{O}$-module of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}
